idiom_name: Promise.all over a readonly tuple / allSettled discriminated union / any + AbortSignal.timeout(ms)
implementation_notes: TypeScript has no runtime of its own, so the fan-out and the gather are JavaScript's promise combinators - but the type system carries the part that matters for the merge: Promise.all over a const tuple preserves the per-recipient result types, and Promise.allSettled returns a discriminated union (status: 'fulfilled' | 'rejected') that forces the aggregation code to narrow each reply before using it. The deadline is AbortSignal.timeout(ms) (or AbortSignal.any to combine a caller abort with the timeout), and no combinator cancels the remaining work, so the losers must be aborted explicitly. This is the default realization; the second variant is for streams that are already observables.
pitfalls: The allSettled union must be narrowed on status: casting it to Offer[] compiles and loses exactly the failure information the gather needs.
Promise.any rejects with AggregateError when every recipient fails, so 'all failed' must be handled distinctly from 'all too slow'.
AbortSignal.timeout cannot be cancelled and keeps its timer (and listeners) alive until it fires; combine it through AbortSignal.any when the caller may abort earlier.

variants.name: RxJS forkJoin / race / combineLatest with the timeout operator
variants.idiom_name: forkJoin(sources) for wait-for-all, race(sources) for first emission, timeout({ each }) for the budget
variants.implementation_notes: Reactive streams express the completeness policies declaratively: forkJoin subscribes to all sources in parallel and emits a single array or object once every source has emitted and completed (the wait-for-all gather, used like Promise.all), race emits from whichever source emits first and unsubscribes the losers, and combineLatest merges partial answers whenever any source updates; the timeout operator ends the gather with a TimeoutError. Choose it when the answers are already observables (websocket feeds, stores) or when the aggregate must keep updating, rather than a one-shot request/response.
pitfalls: forkJoin emits nothing (and errors) if any source errors or never emits, so one silent recipient stalls the whole gather unless each source has its own timeout/catchError.
race unsubscribes the losers, but a cold observable has already started its upstream work: the teardown must actually abort the HTTP call, or the request keeps running.
Subscriptions must be torn down explicitly (take/takeUntil/Unsubscription) or a long-lived gather leaks listeners on every request.
